description: NES accuracy climb (Jank/Broken catalog games fixed on FIX/FIX/FIX vs Mesen). The ROMs are the user's library (X:): the cases skip without it.

cases.description: MMC1 ignores the second (consecutive-cycle) write of a read-modify-write; CPU_FIX's RMW dummy write used to crash the boot (bad opcode 02 at A366). T1 checkpoints match Mesen 2.1.1 (2026-11-16).
SUROM 512 KiB: CHR bank 0 bit 4 picks the PRG half. Used to crash at boot (bad opcode BB). T1 checkpoints match Mesen 2.1.1 (2026-11-16).

MMC5 $5204 in-frame bit drops at line 240 (BIT/BVS wait loop) + 64 KiB WRAM: the strategy map used to ignore every input; now it reaches the province screen. Checked by lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1 (2026-11-16). 2026-11-16 r2: PPU_FIX's vblank dot-skip no longer jumps over line 240's dot 3 (the in-frame drop): the map scroll no longer falls 34 frames behind; nametables/palette/OAM identical to Mesen over 2228 frames.

Trolls on Treasure Island (U): headered 79/vertical, really horizontal (CRC fixup -> 113, as Dudes With Attitude). The world map was built in the hidden nametable; lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1 now matches CIRAM for 1570 frames (2026-11-16).

Sprite overflow with the hardware evaluation bug + OAMADDR held at 0 on dots 257-320 + the OAMADDR>=8 copy over OAM 0-7 at render start: Raid 2020's NMI reads $2002 bit 5 to rotate its sprites (DMA from $2003=$40). OAM/palette identical to Mesen 2.1.1 over 1204 frames (2026-11-16, nes-fix-r2).

Mach Rider (JU): NROM-256 headered horizontal, the cart is vertical (MirroringFixups); as horizontal CIRAM $400-$7FF was never filled. Lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1: nametables 1881 -> 2 different frames of 1885 (2026-11-16).
Hogan's Alley (JU): NROM headered horizontal, the cart is vertical (MirroringFixups). Lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1: nametables 1023 -> 0 different frames of 1024 (2026-11-16).

Rad Racer II (NES-TVROM): four-screen nametables (2 KiB cart VRAM at $2800-$2FFF) were never implemented, so the road scene mirrored onto CIRAM. PPU_FIX now honours iNES byte 6 bit 3. Lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1: nametables 391 -> 1 different frame of 1001 (2026-11-16).

Commando (UNROM, CHR-RAM) writes its title through $2007 with rendering on (lines 25-46 of boot frame 5). PPU_FIX wrote those at v; Mesen 2.1.1 (and the Visual 2C02) writes the address the fetch pipeline has on the PPU bus (its own low byte as data). Now tracked on Mesen's fetch schedule. Lockstep: palette 7 -> 0, CHR-RAM 'differs forever from frame 5' -> 4 frames, nametable 3 -> 2 of 1645 (2026-11-16). Frame 6 picture = Mesen's.

Fire Hawk (mapper 71 BF9097): one-screen select as Mesen 2.1.1's BF909x - a $9000 write enables it, then every $8000-$BFFF write sets it, bit 4 set = screen A. PPU_FIX had A/B swapped and only listened at $9000-$9FFF, so the playfield went to the wrong nametable from frame 297. Lockstep vs Mesen: nametables 2314 -> 3 different frames of 2611 (2026-11-16).

720 (MMC1): the power-on APU frame IRQ stays pending through its $4017=$80 write (no inhibit) and fires right after its CLI at C050. APU_FIX cleared the frame IRQ flag on every $4015 and $4017 write, so the game ran one frame behind Mesen from frame 466. Lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1: nametables 116 -> 0, palette 2 -> 0, OAM 472 -> 0 of 1020 frames (2026-11-16).

T&C Surf Design (CNROM): rendering switched off at line 24 mid sprite evaluation leaves OAMADDR at the evaluator's address plus one (Mesen 2.1.1), so the next vblank OAM DMA lands at 4n+1. PPU_FIX kept OAMADDR 0 and every sprite was a byte off from frame 755. Lockstep vs Mesen: nametables 315 -> 0, OAM 359 -> 0 of 1604 frames (2026-11-16).

Nintendo World Cup (MMC3): a $4015 write must not drop the shared CPU IRQ line unless it clears an APU source. An unconditional RequestIRQ(false) there swallowed pending MMC3 IRQs (lockstep vs Mesen 2.1.1: OAM 45 -> 312 different frames); with the guard it stays at the r4 baseline (2026-11-16).
Castelian: OAM matches Mesen 2.1.1 once APU_FIX keeps the frame IRQ pending through $4015 writes and $4017 writes without the inhibit bit. Lockstep: OAM 454 -> 0 different frames (2026-11-16).
